hook: A fitness tracker says you walked 6 km today, yet you ended the day in your own kitchen, right where you started. Both statements are true. Physics keeps them apart: one number counts every step, the other only asks where you ended up, and the second one comes with a direction.

prereq.q: Which is the SI unit of time?
prereq.why: The SI base units are the meter, the kilogram and the second.

figure.caption: A walk of 5 m out and 2 m back: the distance is 7 m, but the displacement is +3 m, from the start to the end.

chain.cause: You pick an origin and a positive direction
chain.effect: every position along the line becomes one signed number, x, in meters

chain.cause: An object moves from one position to another
chain.effect: its displacement is the final position minus the starting position, with a sign for direction

chain.cause: The object turns around along the way
chain.effect: the distance keeps growing, but parts of the displacement cancel, so the distance is larger

chain.cause: Several displacements happen one after another
chain.effect: their vector sum is found by adding the signed values

ideas: A scalar has a size only (distance, speed, time). A vector has a size and a direction (position, displacement, velocity).
Choose a coordinate system: an origin and a positive direction. Then a position is one signed number, x.
Displacement = final position − starting position. Distance = the total length of the path. They match only for a trip in one direction.
Speed is how fast; velocity is how fast and which way. Along a line the sign of the velocity is the direction of motion.
Add vectors on a line by adding signed values: +320 m and −485 m give −165 m.

misconception.wrong: A negative velocity means the object is slowing down, and a negative position means it is moving backward.
misconception.right: The sign of a velocity only gives the direction of motion: −4.2 m/s means 4.2 m/s in the negative direction. A negative position only says which side of the origin the object is on.

summary: Scalars have a size only; vectors have a size and a direction, which along a line is the sign. Displacement is the final minus the starting position; distance is the path length. Speed is the magnitude of velocity, and vectors on a line add as signed numbers.
